findings.title: Invalid ERB `end if` breaks the best template
findings.body: The conditional opened on line 2 is closed with `<%- end if %>` instead of `<%- end %>`. `end if` is invalid Ruby because the trailing `if` modifier has no expression, so rendering this template for an existing topic raises a SyntaxError and `/embed/best` returns 500 instead of showing the discussion. Controller specs do not render views, so this failure is not caught.

findings.title: RSS item HTML is imported raw without sanitization
findings.body: `poll_feed` passes `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` straight to `TopicEmbed.import`, which creates the post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. `TopicEmbed.import` does not sanitize `contents`, and `app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19` renders `raw post.cooked`. A malicious or compromised feed can therefore inject `<script>` tags or event-handler attributes that execute in the Discourse origin when the embed page loads. The Readability path sanitizes allowed tags and attributes, but the RSS path bypasses that protection; feed HTML needs sanitization before being stored as raw HTML.

findings.title: Non-atomic SETNX/EXPIRE can permanently throttle an embed URL
findings.body: `retrieved_recently?` calls `$redis.setnx` and then a separate `$redis.expire`. If the process dies between those two calls, the key is left without a TTL, so every subsequent attempt for that URL sees it as retrieved and never performs retrieval again. Use an atomic `SET key value EX 60 NX` (or a MULTI/EXEC) so the throttle cannot become permanent.

findings.title: Protocol-relative URLs are rewritten as root-relative
findings.body: The `start_with?('/')` checks at lines 64 and 70 also match protocol-relative URLs such as `//cdn.example.com/a.png`. The code then strips all leading slashes and prefixes the feed host, producing `http://feedhost/cdn.example.com/a.png`, which is wrong and breaks links or images in imported content. Only prefix when there is exactly one leading slash and the URL is not protocol-relative.
